name: ReviewsJet
author: FlexByt, Inc.

sections.description:
ReviewsJet brings the whole review workflow into wp-admin. Connect a platform by
pasting the address of your public page, moderate and reply from one queue, build
a widget with a live preview, and place it with a block.

  • Import from Google, Yelp, Tripadvisor, Trustpilot, Airbnb, Amazon, Etsy, AliExpress and TourRadar, plus reviews left on your own WooCommerce products and reviews you add yourself.
  • Moderate in one queue — publish, hide, pin, tag, reply. Replies are pushed back to the platform the review came from.
  • Display with seven layouts (grid, list, masonry, slider, marquee, quote, popup), customised in WordPress with a live preview.
  • Place with a shortcode anywhere a shortcode goes — a page, a post, a widget area, a page builder.
  • Rank — optional structured data so Google can show star ratings in search results.
  • Ask — send a review request to one customer at a time from the Collect
    screen, optionally attached to a real WooCommerce order.

Widgets are drawn on your pages by the ReviewsJet widget script, which fetches
your published reviews from the ReviewsJet API.

External service

This plugin is the WordPress client for ReviewsJet, a review-management service
at https://reviewsjet.com. A free ReviewsJet account is required. Once you
connect this site, the plugin sends your site address and the reviews, widgets
and settings you manage here to the ReviewsJet API at https://app.reviewsjet.com,
and receives your reviews back.

  • Terms of Service: https://reviewsjet.com/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://reviewsjet.com/privacy

No data is sent anywhere until you connect the plugin to a ReviewsJet workspace.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open ReviewsJet in the WordPress menu.
  3. Click Connect ReviewsJet and approve this site in your ReviewsJet account.

You are never asked for your ReviewsJet password inside WordPress. Approval
happens on reviewsjet.com and this site receives a token scoped to it alone,
which you can revoke at any time from Settings.
sections.faq:
Which review sites can I import from?

Google, Yelp, Tripadvisor, Trustpilot and Airbnb — paste the address of your
public page. Amazon, Etsy, AliExpress and TourRadar reviews come in through the
free ReviewsJet Chrome extension. Reviews on your WooCommerce products, and any
review you add by hand, sit alongside them in the same queue and widgets.

Do I need an API key?

No. Connecting a platform is pasting the address of your public page on it.

Where are my reviews stored?

In ReviewsJet. Widgets on your site are drawn by the ReviewsJet widget
script, which fetches your published reviews from the ReviewsJet API when a
page loads.

Does it work without WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce adds product reviews, a product-page widget, and the option
to attach a real order to a review request; everything else works on any
WordPress site.
sections.changelog:
2.0.1

  • Fixed: connecting a site failed with “ReviewsJet could not be reached” —
    the plugin was calling an API address that no longer exists.
  • Fixed: connecting could fail with “That connection link has expired” after
    reloading the ReviewsJet screen or opening it in a second tab.

2.0.0

  • Rebuilt. Reviews, sources, widgets and settings are now managed inside
    WordPress rather than by linking out to the dashboard — that admin screen
    is now a bundle committed with the plugin (assets/admin/), not a hosted
    page it links out to.
  • Connection now uses a per-site token approved in the dashboard, replacing the
    1.x sign-in that shipped a shared signing secret in the plugin.
  • Widgets are placed with a shortcode. Optional structured data lets Google
    show star ratings in search results.
